newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares dragged lower by options, Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares dragged lower by options, Wall Street.

text.p: Dutch shares closed on the defensive on Wednesday after Wall Street opened lower with markets taking a breather from recent forays to fresh highs.
The AEX index of blue chip stocks ended 1.97 points lower at 590.48, off an early high at 593.16 and below the all-time closing of 592.45, reached on Tuesday.

Dealers said the underlying sentiment in the Dutch market remained bulish but that New York was still the principle driving force short-term. The dollar, which eased a little through the day, removed an early pillar from the market.
"It all looked pretty good this morning but maybe we needed a sideways day after the recent highs," one dealer said.
Analysts said the Dutch market could be running out of steam having put on around 25 percent since the beginning of the year. And the biggest threat came from a correction in the U.S.
But brighter economic prospects in Europe would cushion the blow here, they said, although the repercusions of a fall on Wall Street would certainly impact on the Dutch market.
"I'm not sure thare's a lot of potential left. We could be overdoing a little," said one economist.
"It would hurt the Dutch market," said another.
Analysts predict that the AEX should break through the 600 point level soon -- providing there is no major correction on Wall Street -- and some have medium-term targets of around 610.

But in the short term, dealers said option-holders might keep the index under pressure ahead of the October expiration on Friday, when the 590 level seems to be focus. Some said the level could be lower, as market makers who have sold calls, try to keep them from being exercised and sell shares aggressively.
Philips topped the volume list on Wednesday, losing 0.60 guilders to end at 61.30, reflecting continued investor jitters following the company's shock profit warning on Monday.

Analysts said the news could herald a major shake-up at the electronics giant and some were bracing themselves for massive one-off restructuring charge, when the company announces third quarter results on October 24.
Some said the charge could be as high as one billion guilders as new chairman Cor Boonstra attempts to stamp his mark on the company. Unions fear job losses as high as 5,000.
Elsewhere, flag carrier KLM bucked the trend, putting on 1.30 guilders to 43.90 after increased speculation the airline was about to raise fares to offset spiralling fuel costs.
